# Herdr: coalesce the per-refresh `wl` spawns into one consolidated read

## Problem statement

A Herdr default-view refresh runs **five separate `wl` subprocesses per pane per tick**: the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus the `wl next` browse feed (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Per-spawn Node bootstrap now dominates the cost (~66 % of the remaining 0.70 CPU-s/spawn is the bare-node floor), so F10 capped the achievable reduction at ~65 % with five spawns and missed the 60 % target (47.6 % achieved). The remaining lever is **fewer spawns**: one consolidated read per refresh tick.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** (producer/agent running several Herdr panes on one worklog): wants a responsive worklist without each pane burning CPU on five `wl` boots per tick.
- **Herdr plugin maintainer**: wants one simple, cacheable read seam instead of five coordinated queries with an in-flight memo.
- **wl CLI maintainer**: wants the consolidated command to reuse the existing DB-query and read-cache machinery, not fork it.

### Example user stories

- As a Herdr pane operator, when 4–5 panes refresh every 30 s against one shared worklog, total CPU consumption should drop to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline** so the host stays responsive.
- As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want `fetcher.ts` to issue **one `wl` read per refresh tick** (one DB open, one cache entry), with the displayed items unchanged.
- As an agent relying on the worklist, I want the **mandatory guarantees** (critical items, blocked items and the review queue always shown) preserved by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a **dedicated `wl worklist --json` command** (preferred) or an equivalent `--worklist-bundle` mode, sharing **one DB open and one read-cache entry**.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10): total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s)**, ideally ~5× fewer spawns.
- Cache correctness unchanged: identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
- Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- **Testing/validation:** new tests cover the consolidated command's response shape, read-cache hit and write-invalidation, the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.
- **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Pure read:** the bundle must not write. `wl next`'s auto re-sort is a write byproduct; the bundle must use `--no-re-sort`-style selection (or reuse the selection logic without the write) so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- **Cache reuse:** register the new invocation with the existing read-cache (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`), keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` and fingerprinted by the monotonic state counter; a mid-action write must not cache an unrepresentative payload.
- **Fail-open fallback:** if the consolidated read is unavailable or fails (older `wl`, malformed payload), the fetcher falls back to today's per-subset spawn path with unchanged behaviour.
- **No output change:** the consolidated response must feed the same `extractItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` pipeline so ordering, grouping and audit enrichment are identical.
- **Bounded payload:** the browse feed stays limited by the caller's count; subsets are returned with the same filters (`--root-only` where applicable) so payload growth is bounded and no item duplication is unbounded.
- `--worklog-dir` (module override and per-call) and managed-worktree resolution semantics are unchanged.
- TypeScript/Node stack; match existing style; no new runtime dependency unless unavoidable.

## Existing state

- **fetcher.ts** — `fetchMandatorySubsets()` spawns four `wl list` queries in parallel (critical, review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots); `fetchNextItems()` spawns `wl next` and calls `fetchMandatorySubsets()`, giving five spawns per default-view refresh. An in-flight fetch memo deduplicates *identical* concurrent reads (which collapses the review-queue state query into the review subset), and `fetchChildrenForItems` / `fetchActionableCount` already read in-process from SQLite via one refresh-scoped connection.
- **Read cache** — `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` serve `list`, `next`, `show`, `search` and `status` JSON from a shared on-disk cache keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)`, fingerprinted by a monotonic per-worklog-dir write counter; writes bump the counter and drop entries. `src/cli.ts` performs the lookup before loading the heavy command graph.
- **CLI commands** — `src/commands/*.ts` register subcommands through `src/plugin-types.ts` / `src/command-registry.ts`; `next.ts` owns the auto re-sort and the selection semantics; `list.ts` owns the filtered list queries.
- **Measurement** — `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10, 4 panes × 30 s × 5 s tick, sums per-process CPU from spawn records) and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (spawn-count/latency per refresh).
- **F10 numbers** — pre-F4 baseline 159.44 CPU-s/cycle, after F4–F7 83.58 CPU-s/cycle (47.6 % reduction), target 63.78; per-spawn 1.329 → 0.697 CPU-s against a ~0.46 CPU-s bare-node floor.

## Desired change

1. Add a consolidated worklist read to the `wl` CLI — preferably a new `wl worklist --json` command — that opens the database **once** and returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload, built from the same query/selection code the individual commands use.
2. Make it a cacheable read invocation (one cache entry, same state-counter fingerprint and write invalidation), so repeat refreshes across panes hit the cache as a single entry.
3. Change `fetcher.ts` so the default-view refresh drives that one read (with the review-queue state and browse feed derived from it) and retains the existing per-subset path as a fail-open fallback.
4. Add coverage: command unit/integration tests, cache hit/invalidation tests, fetcher single-spawn and mandatory-guarantee tests, and an output-parity test against the per-subset path; update the spawn-reduction simulation and the benchmark expectations.
5. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and any CLI reference docs/comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — **new** consolidated read command (or a `--worklist-bundle` mode added to `src/commands/list.ts`)
- `src/command-registry.ts` — register the new command
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add the invocation to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` / cacheability checks
- `src/cli.ts` — cache lookup path (expected unchanged; verify the new command is served before the heavy graph)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single consolidated read, review-state/browse derivation, fail-open fallback
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring so the bundle replaces the per-subset fan-out
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — spawn-reduction simulation uses the consolidated invocation
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-*.test.ts` — mandatory-subset, review-queue and output-parity coverage
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — measurement harness (expects the consolidated query)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section updated

## Related work

- **F10 — WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** (completed): measured the <= 60 % shortfall and filed this item with the spawn-count lever. This item is the follow-up implementation of that lever.
- **WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B** (completed, outbound dependency): spawn-load epic — transient `wl` process CPU usage.
- **WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** (completed): cut cold refresh cost — in-process SQLite reads, in-flight fetch memo, batched expanded children. The consolidated read builds on this.
- **WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B** (completed): one shared in-process connection per refresh — related "one open per refresh" precedent.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** (completed): make Herdr refresh snappy after agent updates — parent of the earlier performance work.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md`, `docs/benchmarks/wal-read-latency-benchmark.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cache staleness (risk, high):** a single cache entry must never serve stale data across a write. Mitigation: reuse the counter fingerprint, cache only when the counter is unchanged since lookup, and add an explicit write-invalidation test.
- **Re-sort write byproduct (risk, medium):** today's `wl next` runs an auto re-sort (a DB write) on some invocations. The bundle must be a pure read; assumption: `--no-re-sort` selection produces the same displayed order for a stable DB. Verify with an output-parity test; if ordering genuinely differs, resolve the re-sort as a separate, explicitly-documented concern rather than making the bundle a write.
- **Mandatory-subset regression (risk, high):** a bundle that silently drops a subset breaks the always-shown guarantees. Mitigation: tests assert each mandatory subset is present regardless of the browse window.
- **Backwards compatibility (risk, low):** an older `wl` without the new command. Mitigation: fall back to the per-subset spawn path (fail-open).
- **Cross-subset consistency (risk, medium):** the five subsets are read in one process but through separate queries; a write landing mid-bundle could make the subsets disagree. Mitigation: serve all subsets from one DB connection inside a read transaction (or the same store snapshot) so the payload reflects one stable state; at minimum, match today's eventual-consistency behaviour and document it.
- **Payload size (risk, low):** five subsets in one payload. Mitigation: keep the browse feed count-bounded and reuse the existing dedupe/merge pipeline.
- **Scope creep (risk, medium):** further per-spawn startup optimisation (F4–F7) is out of scope. Record additional opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** `wl` and the Herdr plugin ship together from this repository, so the fetcher may rely on the new command in the same release; the fallback remains for robustness.

## Verification plan

```sh
# CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle, 4 panes (F10 harness)
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh -- --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5

# Spawn count and latency for a single default-view refresh
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json
```

- Compare the measured CPU-seconds against the ≤ 63.8 CPU-s target and the pre-F4 baseline quoted above.
- Run the changed-scope and full test suites via `/skill:test`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Was an interview needed for this intake?
  **A (agent, based on repo evidence):** No. The seed context already contains a measured problem, a quantified target, explicit acceptance criteria and a named lever, so the brief was drafted directly from that plus a repo inspection. Source: work item description and F10 comment.
- **Q:** Which command shape should the consolidated read take?
  **A (agent, derived from work item AC):** The AC permits either a `--worklist-bundle` mode or a dedicated command; this brief records a dedicated `wl worklist --json` command as the preferred option (cleaner cache key, no change to `list`/`next` semantics). Source: work item AC 1.
- **Q:** Does the browse feed's auto re-sort write belong in the bundle?
  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The bundle must be a pure read to be deterministically cacheable, so it uses `--no-re-sort`-style selection and the re-sort is treated as a separate concern; output parity is guarded by a test. Recorded as a risk above. Source: `src/commands/next.ts` auto re-sort logic.
- **Q:** Is a fail-open fallback required?
  **A (agent, derived from existing fetcher design):** Yes — the fetcher's existing in-process fast paths all fail open to `wl` spawns; the consolidated read follows the same convention. Source: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** – Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle (completed)
- **WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9** – [test-failure] read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19** – Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, always, bare, baseline, behaviour (+101 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: always, bare, baseline, behaviour, bench (+92 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: achieved, always, bare, behaviour, blocked (+86 more)

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-21T11:11Z** — `plan` skill (agent `plan`, session `herdr-1792579182-3452759-11361`) decomposed the item into **six** child features in test-first dependency order:
  `WL-0MVI0HH740065Z2T` (verification harness) → `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` (`wl worklist` command) → {`WL-0MVI0IS6Y0028KTO` (read cache), `WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78` (fetcher + fallback)} → `WL-0MVI0IW8V007DFM6` (`doRefresh` wiring) → `WL-0MVI0IX6E000N6IZ` (docs + benchmark evidence). Dependency edges wired to match.
- **2026-10-21T11:18Z** — Acceptance Criteria section converted from a numbered list to a bullet list so the shared `tree_coverage` helper parses all 8 parent ACs (a numbered list parsed as zero ACs, making the coverage review vacuous). Each child gained explicit `Traceability to parent AC<n>` acceptance bullets. Coverage review result: **8/8 parent ACs covered, 0 uncovered, 0 conflicts, action `proceed`**; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.
- **2026-10-21T11:20Z** — Effort/risk refreshed for the decomposed plan: effort **Small** (expected 8.66 h, recommended 12.66 h), risk **Medium** (score 9/25), confidence 92% (comment `WL-C0MVI0U0F6009D0CW`).

## Appendix: Plan session questions & answers (2026-10-21)

- **Q:** Does planning need a new interview round?
  **A (agent, repo evidence):** No. The intake Appendix already settled the command shape (`wl worklist --json`), the pure-read/`--no-re-sort` treatment, and the fail-open fallback. The effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk High) and the approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (approval is requested only for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk), so no producer confirmation pause was required. Source: `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` and `plan-approval-gate` output, 2026-10-21T11:0xZ.
- **Q:** Does the consolidated read also serve the stage-filtered and priority-filtered worklist views?
  **A (agent, derived from parent AC2 and `fetchItemsForView`):** No. Parent AC2 scopes the change to the *default-view refresh tick*; the stage, priority and recent-dispatches views keep their existing reads. Recorded as an explicit acceptance criterion in `WL-0MVI0IW8V007DFM6`.
- **Q:** How is browse-feed parity with `wl next` guaranteed without its auto re-sort write?
  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The command performs `--no-re-sort`-style selection (never calls `reSort`) and parity is enforced by an output-parity test comparing the bundle path and the per-subset path on the same DB state (`WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78`). The re-sort remains a separate, explicitly-documented concern as recorded in the intake risks.
- **Q:** Where does the browse-feed selection logic live so `next.ts` is not forked?
  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The post-`findNextWorkItems` pipeline (child-count/audit enrichment, group assignment and group sort) is extracted into a shared module consumed by both `next` and the new `worklist` command (`WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF`, reusing `assignItemGroups`/`compareGroupedItems` from `src/commands/grouping.ts`).
- **Q:** How is the "one DB open" requirement verified rather than assumed?
  **A (agent, design decision):** A spy/counter test asserts exactly one database handle is opened per `wl worklist` invocation, and a separate test asserts the command never bumps the read-cache state counter (pure read). Recorded as acceptance criteria in `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF`.
- **OPEN QUESTION:** none outstanding. The `Traceability to parent AC<n>` bullets added to child items are coverage traceability, not additional scope.

## Goal

As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want the performance harnesses and shared test fixtures ready to measure and verify a single consolidated `wl` read, so that the spawn-reduction target (parent AC3) is measurable before the consolidated command exists and every later slice can be tested without re-inventing fixtures.

This is the test-first slice of parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS: it adds measurement/verification infrastructure only and changes no production behaviour.

## Scope

- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` currently hard-code the five-query legacy set (`QUERIES`). Add a query-set selector (`--query-set legacy|consolidated`, default `legacy`) so the same harness measures one consolidated invocation per refresh tick while keeping the historical numbers comparable. In C1 the `consolidated` path is plumbing only: it must degrade cleanly (a clear "invocation not available yet" report/no-op, non-zero exit only when explicitly requested) because `wl worklist` does not exist until WL-C2.
- Add a reusable seeded-worklog fixture helper for the new CLI and herdr tests: root and child items spanning critical / in_review (completed + in-progress) / blocked / in-progress / open non-critical, at least one with a stored audit result, and at least one child under a root so `--root-only` filters are provably exercised.
- Extend `tests/bench/herdr-refresh-perf.test.ts` (or add a focused sibling) to cover the query-set selector plumbing and the consolidated-vs-legacy baseline ratio computation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` accepts `--query-set legacy` (default) and `--query-set consolidated`, issues exactly one invocation per tick in `consolidated` mode, and reports spawn counts / CPU-seconds for whichever set is selected.
- `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` accepts the same selector and reports spawn count and latency for the selected set.
- An invalid `--query-set` value exits non-zero with an explicit error naming the valid values.
- The `consolidated` set is defined from a single exported constant so the CLI invocation vector lives in one place (no duplicated argv in bench and tests).
- A shared seeded-worklog fixture helper exists and is reused by at least one test, seeding the subset mix above (verified by assertions on the seeded data: ≥1 critical, ≥1 completed/in_review, ≥1 in-progress/in_review, ≥1 blocked root, ≥1 open non-critical, ≥1 child item).
- The reduction ratio is computed from a measured legacy baseline, not a hard-coded constant, and a test asserts the ratio arithmetic (e.g. 5 → 1 spawn yields 80 % reduction).
- No production source file (`src/`, `packages/herdr/src/` excluding tests) changes behaviour in this slice.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC3: measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10), total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to ≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s), ideally ~5× fewer spawns; this slice supplies the measurement harness for that comparison.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC8: the full project test suite must pass with the new changes; this slice keeps the suite green and documents its target.

## Minimal implementation

1. Export `LEGACY_WORKLIST_QUERIES` and `CONSOLIDATED_WORKLIST_QUERY` (single `worklist` argv) from one shared location importable by bench and tests.
2. Add `--query-set` parsing to both harnesses with validation and default `legacy`.
3. Route the tick loop through the selected set; in `consolidated` mode collect a clear "unavailable" diagnostic instead of a hard crash when the command is absent.
4. Factor the CPU/spawn summary maths into a helper that takes baseline and candidate measurements.
5. Add the seeded-worklog fixture helper next to the existing `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` helpers.
6. Add/extend bench tests for the selector and ratio arithmetic; update each harness's header doc comment.

## Key Files

- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — add `--query-set` selector, single-invocation consolidated tick
- `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` — add `--query-set` selector and consolidated reporting
- `tests/bench/herdr-refresh-perf.test.ts` — selector + ratio arithmetic coverage
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — seeded-worklog fixture helper
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — consumes the shared query-set constants (no new assertions yet)

## Dependencies

- None (first slice).

## Deliverables

- Harness selector + shared query-set constants.
- Seeded-worklog fixture helper.
- Bench plumbing tests.
- Updated harness doc comments explaining the two query sets and the target ratio.

## Notes

- Keep the default `legacy` set byte-identical to today's five queries so F10's recorded numbers (159.44 → 83.58 CPU-s/cycle) remain comparable.
- Do not raise the 300 s budget in `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`; the consolidated path is expected to shorten that run, not lengthen it.

## Goal

As a wl CLI maintainer, I want a dedicated `wl worklist --json` read command that returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload from **one DB open**, built from the same query and selection code the individual commands use, so that Herdr can issue one read per refresh tick instead of five.

## Scope

Parent AC1 (command half). This slice delivers the command plus its tests; caching is WL-C3 and the fetcher consumer is WL-C4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl worklist --json` exists and is registered as a built-in command (present in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES`, its lazy loader map, and the help metadata), with `--number/-n` (browse-feed count, default 20) and `--prefix` options.
- Its JSON payload contains five named subsets — `critical`, `reviewQueue`, `inProgressRoots`, `blockedRoots`, `browse` — plus payload metadata (at minimum the resolved worklog dir and the browse count requested). Each subset key is **always present**, as an empty array rather than omitted, when it has no members.
- The four list subsets use exactly the existing filters: critical = `--priority critical --status open,in-progress,blocked,completed` (all parent levels); review queue = `--status completed,in-progress --stage in_review --root-only`; in-progress roots = `--status in-progress --root-only`; blocked roots = `--status blocked --root-only`.
- The `browse` subset matches `wl next -n <count> --include-in-progress --include-blocked --no-re-sort --json` item-for-item and order-for-order for the same DB state, including the audit (`auditResult`, `auditedAt`), `childCount` and group (`group`, `groupLabel`) enrichment that `wl next` emits.
- The command opens the database **exactly once** per invocation (asserted by a spy/counter test) and issues all five reads against that single handle.
- The command is a **pure read**: it never calls `reSort` and never bumps the read-cache state counter (asserted by comparing the counter file before/after).
- The browse feed is bounded by the requested count; mandatory subsets are returned unfiltered by that count.
- `--worklog-dir` (global option) works unchanged, and no item appears in `browse` that would not appear in `wl next` for the same arguments.
- Duplication is avoided by extracting the browse-feed selection + enrichment currently inline in `src/commands/next.ts` into a shared helper called by **both** `next` and `worklist` (no forked selection logic).
- New tests cover: payload shape with an empty DB, payload shape with the seeded fixture, per-subset filter parity against the equivalent `wl list` invocation, browse-feed parity against `wl next --no-re-sort`, single DB open, and pure-read behaviour.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC1: a single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a dedicated `wl worklist --json` command, sharing one DB open.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC6/AC8: new tests cover the consolidated command's response shape and output parity with the per-subset path; the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extract `next`'s post-`findNextWorkItems` pipeline (childCounts + audit enrichment, group assignment when count > 1, group sort) into a shared module used by `next.ts` and the new command.
2. Add `src/commands/worklist.ts` registering `worklist`, resolving the DB once via `utils.getDatabase()`, running the four `db.list()` subset queries and the shared browse-feed selection, then emitting one `output.json()` payload.
3. Register the command in `src/command-registry.ts` and the help-group metadata in `src/cli-main.ts`.
4. Apply the `--no-re-sort` contract in code (never invoke `reSort`) and document it in the command description.
5. Add `tests/cli/worklist-command.test.ts` covering the criteria above using the WL-C1 seeded fixture.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — **new** consolidated read command
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — **new** shared browse-feed selection/enrichment extracted from `next.ts`
- `src/commands/next.ts` — consume the extracted helper (behaviour unchanged)
- `src/command-registry.ts` — register `worklist` loader
- `src/cli-main.ts` — help grouping metadata for `worklist`
- `tests/cli/worklist-command.test.ts` — **new** command tests
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — seeded fixture (from WL-C1)

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C1 (shared fixtures + query-set constants).

## Deliverables

- `wl worklist --json` command with documented payload contract.
- Shared browse-feed selection helper (no duplicated selection logic).
- Command test suite covering shape, filter parity, browse parity, single open and pure-read.

## Notes

- Payload contract sketch: `{ success, worklogDir, requestedCount, subsets: { critical: [...], reviewQueue: [...], inProgressRoots: [...], blockedRoots: [...], browse: [...] } }`. Keep it stable — WL-C3 caches it verbatim and WL-C4 parses it.
- Do **not** fold stage/priority filtered views into the bundle; those remain separate reads (out of scope per parent AC2's "default-view refresh tick").
- Record the final payload contract in a comment on this item before marking in_review so WL-C4 can rely on it.

data.description:
## Goal

As a wl CLI maintainer, I want the new `wl worklist --json` invocation served from and backfilled into the existing on-disk read cache as a single cache entry, so repeat refreshes across Herdr panes hit the cache once per refresh instead of per subset.

## Scope

Parent AC1 (cache half) and AC4 (cache correctness).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `worklist` is added to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` and `isCacheableReadCommand('worklist')` returns true.
- A cacheable `wl worklist --json` invocation is served from cache on repeat with an unchanged DB: second invocation records a `cache-hit` spawn (`recordSpawn('cache-hit')`) and performs no DB work.
- A write (create/update/sync/comment…) bumps the state counter and invalidates the worklist entry; the next invocation does real read work and reflects the new DB state.
- The payload is keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` exactly like the other read commands — a different `--worklog-dir` or different `-n` count is a distinct entry.
- A mid-action write is not cached: when the state counter changes between lookup and `onJsonOutput`, the payload is not stored (same guard as today's commands).
- `WL_CACHE_DISABLED=1` disables both lookup and backfill for `worklist`.
- The cache serves the new command before the heavy command graph loads (the existing `src/cli.ts` preAction lookup path covers it; no new fast-path exception).
- New tests in `tests/cli/` cover: hit-on-repeat, invalidation-on-write, distinct keys for distinct `--worklog-dir`, and the disable env var.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC1: the consolidated `wl worklist --json` invocation is served as one read-cache entry.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC4: cache correctness unchanged — identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC6: new tests cover read-cache hit and write-invalidation for the consolidated command.

## Minimal implementation

## Goal

As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want the default-view refresh to issue **one** `wl` read per tick — `wl worklist --json` — with the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root and blocked-root guarantees preserved and a fail-open fallback to today's per-subset spawn path when the consolidated read is unavailable.

## Scope

Parent AC2 (single read), AC5 (output parity), AC6 (fetcher tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fetchNextItems(count)` for a default-view refresh issues exactly **one** `runWl` invocation (`worklist`) when the command is available; no `wl list` or `wl next` spawns are issued for the bundle path (the in-flight fetch memo is bypassed for the bundle, or dedupes it, with no extra spawns).
- The mandatory subsets are derived from the bundle: all critical, all in_review (completed + in-progress), all in-progress roots and all blocked roots appear in the returned list regardless of the browse count (existing mandatory-guarantee tests still pass).
- `fetchReviewQueueState()` is derived from the bundle's `reviewQueue` subset (completed-only count + `auditsOutstanding`) and returns the same value as today's standalone `wl list` query for the same DB state.
- Audit enrichment is preserved: for items shared with mandatory `wl list` subsets, the richer `wl list`-style audit fields (`auditResult`, `auditedAt`, `fingerprint`, `currentFingerprint`) win over the `browse` representation, exactly as today (WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G).
- Output parity: for the same DB state, the bundle path's final `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` output is identical to today's per-subset path (test compares both pipelines on the seeded fixture).
- Fail-open: when `wl worklist` is unavailable (older `wl`, non-zero exit, malformed/unparseable payload, missing subset key), the fetcher falls back to the existing per-subset spawns with byte-identical behaviour — the fallback path is asserted by a test that mocks the bundle failure.
- `wl next`'s auto re-sort is NOT triggered by the bundle (pure read); no write byproduct, so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- `--worklog-dir` and managed-worktree resolution behave unchanged (existing worktree tests still pass).
- New tests cover: single-spawn assertion, mandatory-subset presence, review-queue derivation, output parity, and fail-open fallback.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC2: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC5: Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC6: new tests cover the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `worklist` to the fetcher's `MEMOIZABLE_COMMANDS` set (bundle is a cacheable read; memo dedupes identical concurrent refreshes — same as today).
2. Add `fetchWorklistBundle()` that runs `runWl(['worklist', '-n', String(count)])`, extracts the five subsets with `extractItems`, and validates the shape (unknown-shape ⇒ fail-open).
3. Rework `fetchNextItems(count)` to: try the bundle → derive mandatory sets + review-queue state + browse feed → merge/enrich with the existing `WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G` logic → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems`; on any failure, fall back to today's `Promise.all([runWl(next), fetchMandatorySubsets()])` exactly.
4. Rework `fetchReviewQueueState()` to read the bundle's `reviewQueue` subset when already fetched in the same refresh, falling back to the standalone query.
5. Add `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` with injected fake `execFileAsync` covering the criteria.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchWorklistBundle`, reworked `fetchNextItems`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, memo set
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — **new** bundle tests
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-review-queue.test.ts`, `fetcher-include-blocked.test.ts`, `fetcher-inprocess.test.ts` — existing guarantees must keep passing
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — seeded fixture (from WL-C1)

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C2 (`wl worklist` command + payload contract) and WL-C3 (cacheability).
- Depends on WL-C1 only transitively via WL-C2 (fixtures land in WL-C1; tests here reuse them).

## Deliverables

- Single-spawn default-view refresh with preserved mandatory guarantees.
- Review-queue state derived from the bundle.
- Fail-open fallback path.
- Fetcher test coverage including output parity.

## Notes

- Keep the browse feed bounded by the caller's count; mandatory subsets stay unfiltered by count.
- The re-sort write-byproduct risk (parent risk, medium) is handled by the command's `--no-re-sort`-style selection (WL-C2) plus this slice's output-parity test; if parity genuinely differs, record it as a comment and resolve separately rather than making the bundle a write.

## Goal

As a Herdr pane operator, I want `doRefresh` to run the whole default-view refresh from the single consolidated read — items, review-queue banner state and actionable context — so a refresh tick costs one `wl` process instead of five per pane.

## Scope

Parent AC2 (wire-through), AC5 (unchanged output), AC6 (worklist-level tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A default-view `doRefresh` cycle issues exactly **one** `wl` spawn for worklist data (asserted by a spawn-count integration test with an injected exec seam), down from five.
- The review-queue banner state (`applySprintState`) is populated from the same consolidated read — no separate review-queue spawn on the default view.
- Filtered views are unchanged: the stage-filtered (`fetchItemsByStage`), priority-filtered (`fetchItemsByPriority`) and recent-dispatches paths still use their existing reads, and the `activeDispatchFilter` path still merges live items from the default fetcher.
- Expanded-parent children still render correctly across the swap (no collapse flicker): the batched in-process children read continues to run concurrently with the consolidated item read, and the existing expand-across-refresh test passes.
- Idle behaviour is preserved: a refresh with no change still spawns zero `wl` processes where it did before (no new unconditional read).
- Event-loop responsiveness: the ≤ 100 ms p95 input-lag guard test still passes.
- Fail-open at the TUI layer: when the consolidated read fails, the refresh shows the per-subset fallback result (or the previous list) instead of an empty or errored view.
- New/extended tests cover the single-spawn default view, derived banner state, and unchanged filtered-view behaviour.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC2: the default-view refresh issues that single read per default-view refresh tick and the mandatory-subset guarantees are preserved by tests.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC5: Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state; existing fetcher tests and the spawn-reduction simulation pass.

## Minimal implementation

1. In `doRefresh`, replace the `fetchReviewQueueState()` + `fetchItemsForView(...)` default-path pair with one consolidated fetch that yields both the items and the review-queue state (e.g. `fetchWorklistBundle()` returns `{ items, reviewState, actionableCount? }`).
2. Keep the children fetch (`fetchChildrenForItems`) concurrent with the consolidated read via the existing `InProcessRefreshScope`.
3. Keep `fetchItemsForView` for the filtered/dispatch views; only the unfiltered default path changes.
4. Extend the worklist refresh test(s) with a spawn-count assertion using the injected `setExecFileAsync` seam.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring, `applySprintState` input
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — bundle result shape consumed by `doRefresh` (from WL-C4)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-*.test.ts` — single-spawn + banner + filtered-view coverage
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — must keep passing

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C4 (fetcher bundle + fail-open fallback).

## Deliverables

- Default-view refresh driven by one consolidated read.
- Banner state derived from the same read.
- Single-spawn and unchanged-filtered-view test coverage.

## Notes

- "One spawn" means one **worklist-data** spawn per tick. The in-process SQLite reads (children, actionable count) are already zero-spawn and stay that way.
- Do not reorder or bypass `doRefresh`'s typing gate, visibility gate, single-flight guard or trailing coalescing.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the documentation and measured benchmark evidence updated to describe the consolidated read, so the next engineer can see what changed, why, the measured CPU reduction against the F10 baseline, and how to reproduce it.

## Scope

Parent AC3 (measurement evidence) and AC7 (documentation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` § "Cold-refresh cost" describes the consolidated read: one `wl worklist --json` per default-view tick, one read-cache entry, review-queue/browse derivation, the fail-open fallback, and that filtered views are unchanged.
- `CLI.md` documents `wl worklist` — purpose, options (`-n/--number`, `--prefix`), JSON payload shape (five subsets + metadata), pure-read/cacheable guarantee, and a usage example.
- Inline doc comments in `src/commands/worklist.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts` (`READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` comment) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` reflect the new path, cross-referencing the same rationale as the docs.
- The measured spawn count per default-view refresh is recorded in the doc (expected 5 → 1) and produced by the harness, not hand-waved.
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts --query-set consolidated --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5` is executed and its CPU-seconds-per-cycle result is recorded on this work item and in the doc, compared against the pre-F4 baseline (159.44 CPU-s) and the F10 target (≤ 63.78 CPU-s).
- `npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json` spawn count and latency for a single default-view refresh are recorded on this work item.
- If the measured result misses the ≤ 0.4× target, the shortfall is documented with the measured number and an explicit follow-up note (no unsupported claims).
- Documentation mentions the backwards-compatibility fallback (older `wl` without the command) and the cross-subset consistency approach (one connection) including its residual risk.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC3: measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10), total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to ≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s), ideally ~5× fewer spawns; this slice records the measured evidence.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC7: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC8: the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` § 3 (Cold-refresh cost) with the consolidated-read bullet, revised spawn count and the new measured numbers.
2. Add the `wl worklist` entry to `CLI.md` (command reference + payload contract).
3. Update the header comments of the touched source modules.
4. Run both benchmarks with the consolidated query set, capture the JSON output, and paste the summary numbers into this work item as a comment plus the doc.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section
- `CLI.md` — command reference for `wl worklist`
- `src/commands/worklist.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — doc comments
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts`, `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` — measurement source (from WL-C1)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — refresh-cost note if it references spawn counts

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C5 (the wired refresh must exist before it can be measured).

## Deliverables

- Updated dev doc and CLI reference.
- Recorded benchmark evidence (CPU-seconds/cycle, spawn count, latency) with the comparison table.
- Comment on this item carrying the raw benchmark summary.

## Notes

- Follow the background-job etiquette for the benchmark runs (launch → prepare docs → one completion-aware wait → collect); do not poll with fixed `sleep`.
- Measurement must use the pre-compiled CLI (`dist/cli.js` or the bundled snapshot), not `tsx src/cli.ts` per spawn, or the numbers will not be comparable to F10's.
